elements.name: Lens (Rive camera lens with a 9-blade Klein iris, the first-visit opener)
elements.what: Layers back to front inside .kl__lens (Lens.tsx:233-238): the film circle .kl__film (inset 14.6%, border-radius 50%, HeroMedia with LENS_FILM, sizes '(max-width: 860px) 62vw, 440px'), the static rest frame and closed frame (inline SVG via ?raw so they are never LCP candidates, 19-20, 235-236), and the Rive canvas (237). Rive draws barrel, focus ring, knurling, 9 blades, glass; the page drives blade 0's corners/light (10 numbers v0x..g1y) and 'focus' through data binding every frame (NAMES 49, write 71-76); blades 1-8 are blade 0 rotated 40deg inside the file. Geometry is shared with the static frames (lens-geometry.js LENS n=9, rl=330, rBig=440, rOut=486, rest aperture 0.72 at :20; twistFor :24-26; blade() :30-46). Motion model: aperture a on a damped spring (damping 0.78, 1/240 s substeps, Lens.tsx:90-111); targets (77-88): intro closed 0.28 s (k 300) then fully open until 0.95 s (k 260) then rest, sessionStorage 'mw-hero-iris' written at that moment (remember, :30, :84); pointer over lens (fine pointer only, touch ignored, 126-135) opens to 0.92 and turns blades toward the pointer; tap/click inside the circle = 150 ms shutter to 0.03 (136-143); scroll progress opens toward 1 (86-87, ScrollTrigger on closest section top top->bottom top, 197-200). Draws only while moving and on screen: sleep() stops rendering two frames after settling (120-123), IntersectionObserver stops it off screen (201-206), ResizeObserver redraws once (207-212). FIRST-VISIT GATE: index.html:42-57 runs before first paint and adds html.hero-iris only if not prerender, not OS reduced motion (unless ?motion=full), not ?reduce=1, path '/', and no sessionStorage 'mw-hero-iris'; 10 s safety timeout removes it. CSS hero-lens.css:30-31 then shows lens-closed.svg instead of lens-rest.svg. Lens.tsx: with the class it starts Rive on the very next animation frame (193, not idle); without it after load + idle (194, afterLoadAndIdle 32-47, idle timeout 2500). Rive: dynamic import('@rive-app/canvas-lite') (146), artboard 'Lens', state machine 'Main', autoBind, Rive listeners off, touch-scroll allowed, Fit.Contain; DPR capped at 2 (158). onLoad validates all 10 view-model numbers, else cleans up and stays SVG (162); the opening plays only if the lens is on screen and not CALM (164-166); canvas is shown (data-live, CSS 32-33) only after two rAFs so the first drawn frame equals the SVG pose (169-183). SVG FALLBACK: Rive load error, or Rive not ready within 4.5 s on a first visit (190: gaveUp -> endIntro -> rest SVG; a late Rive is discarded, never starts late); REDUCE/prerender: endIntro and rest SVG only (60). Dev hook window.__lens (216).
elements.mobile: At 390 the lens is 335px; film circle ~237px showing lens-m.mp4 (600px encode). No pointer hover/turn on touch; tap = shutter. Scroll opens the iris and HeroLens scales it 1.16. Rive canvas surface = 335 x DPR(<=2) = 670px square.
elements.reduced: REDUCE: rest SVG, no Rive, no listeners. CALM: never gets html.hero-iris (index.html:46), Rive loads after load+idle and starts at rest; pointer, shutter and scroll aperture stay (visitor-driven). No JS: rest SVG (stills are in the markup).
elements.perf: lens.riv 19 KB; canvas-lite wasm ~0.9 MB in the shared 'rive' manual chunk (vite.config.ts:66), shared with hero.riv and companion.riv so it downloads once per page. Two inline SVGs ~4.3 KB each in the JS. On a first visit the wasm fetch starts at the first frame, competing with the LCP font on slow phones (measured LCP 2.39 s was with this). rAF loop only while the spring moves; zero cost at rest.
elements.api: export function Lens({ engine }: { engine: MotionEngine | null }). Classes .kl__lens, .kl__film, .kl__still(--rest|--closed), .kl__rive, [data-live]; global html.hero-iris; sessionStorage key 'mw-hero-iris'. Geometry exports LENS, twistFor(a, extra), blade(a, t). Regenerate the .riv and both SVGs with npm run rive:lens (build-lens.mjs) - never hand-edit.
elements.reuse_in_one_shot: 390 first: the lens becomes a real camera lens lying on the hero sheet, the hero's only picture. Size ~248-280px (min(72vw, 300px)), centred on the sheet's top edge so ~35% of it overhangs onto the grey desk and casts a short desk shadow - it reads as an object resting on the paper, and its circle is still the Horizon disc (#64). H1 + sub + CTA sit on the paper below it in their own text zone (never under the lens). The film keeps playing inside it (that is where the sacred lens.mp4/lens-m.mp4 lives; do not move the film into a laptop screen, #60 'laptop inside a laptop'). Drive the iris from the camera instead of the hero-section trigger: at the overview the iris is at rest, and as the dive lands (dive() timeline progress) it opens to 1 'the camera focuses on your business'; keep the first-visit closed->open->rest intro and the tap shutter unchanged. Needed changes: (1) let Lens take an optional progress source (e.g. a `trigger`/`range` prop or an imperative setProgress) instead of el.closest('section') top->bottom (197-200), because inside a 210svh sticky hold that range is the whole hold; (2) regenerate lens.riv/SVGs with a desk palette for the outer shadow ring (lens-rest.svg uses #00061E/#00113D navy stops tuned to the night stage; on #ECEEF1 it shows as a navy halo) and give .kl__film a shot token instead of var(--stage) (hero-lens.css:24); (3) remove HeroLens's own scale tween when the lens sits inside the dive model. Desktop: same object, larger (min(36vw, 460px)), placed at the sheet's start side beside the copy.
elements.risks: Name clash: src/look/shot/camera.ts:9 exports `LENS = 1100` (perspective) while lens-geometry exports `LENS` (iris constants) - import one under an alias. If the shot hero keeps html.hero-iris but the lens is not on screen at load (sheet below the overview fold at 390), onLoad skips the opening and does not call remember(), so the intro is retried on the next load - acceptable but the 10 s class timeout and closed SVG must not show a closed iris to someone who scrolls fast (CSS swaps to rest only when data-live or the class drops). The iris pointer-turn math assumes an untransformed circle; under rotateX/rotateZ of the dive, getBoundingClientRect returns the projected box, so hover/shutter hit-testing drifts during the dive (harmless, but test).
elements.a11y: Entirely aria-hidden (233-237), decorative; the shutter is pointer-only and carries no meaning. data-zone='art'.

elements.name: Companion: the Rive laptop that writes the message (contract-bound)
elements.what: span.ct__pal (aria-hidden, data-zone=art) holding the CSS rest-pose (companion-rest.svg, 330x216) and a . With the engine present and not PRERENDER/REDUCE, an IntersectionObserver (rootMargin 600px) triggers afterLoadAndIdle, which dynamically imports @rive-app/canvas-lite. That creates new Rive (artboard 'Companion', state machine 'Main', autoBind, Fit.Contain, shouldDisableRiveListeners, isTouchScrollEnabled) and sets the wasm URL. On load it writes VM prefersReducedMotion = engine.CALM, the status enum and the progress number, then shows the canvas after two rAFs (data-live) and renders only while on screen (Companion.tsx:59-111). Effects push status, progress and the keystroke trigger. Contract: VM 'Companion' with status enum {idle, typing, loading, sent, error}, progress 0-100, keystroke trigger, prefersReducedMotion bool. States: idle = half-bright page; typing = lines write RTL with caret; loading = lines fold into the Horizon line inside a disc and slosh 3deg; sent = level fills to the exact Horizon mark; error = lines return with a red dot. No events back to the app. Colours (build-scene.mjs:24-28): lid #0E0E10, black screen, white ink, words #8E9CC8, logo #FFFFFF/#6E8CFF, aluminium base gradient #E6E6E9 to #6E6E73, error #FF6961.
elements.mobile: Aspect 330/216. Width clamp(176px,38%,232px), so 176px at 390, which is small for the 'wow' object. The canvas resizes through a ResizeObserver.
elements.reduced: REDUCE never loads Rive; the SVG rest pose stays (identical pose, so no swap). CALM loads Rive with prefersReducedMotion=true: no slosh, no blink, but state changes still play. Off screen: stopRendering.
elements.perf: About 0.9MB wasm plus a 7KB .riv in their own 'rive' chunk, loaded only after load + idle and within 600px of the viewport. Canvas2D. Note: the hero (Lens) also uses Rive; if both pages share the runtime, the wasm is cached.
elements.api: Default export Companion({ engine: MotionEngine|null, status: CompanionStatus, progress: number, keys: number }) and type CompanionStatus. Class .ct__pal[data-live]. Build: npm run rive:companion (generator, then rive CLI, then copy). Probe: rive-probe.mjs --contract. Never hand-edit cli/scene.rml.
elements.reuse_in_one_shot: This IS 'the laptop' Nati wants kept, and it is already defined as 'the hero's laptop' (#56). On the desk it is the laptop sitting at the head of the contact letter, drawn at 232-256px at 390 and slightly overlapping the sheet. Optional continuity: the same laptop silhouette appears small, closed or static, in the opening overview of the desk (CSS Laptop or the rest SVG), and the camera 'finds' it again at the end when the visitor types. If the night screen clashes with the paper world, change only COL in build-scene.mjs (for example ink 1B1D21 on a FFFFFF screen, words 4A4F57, logo 0E1016/002FA7, the light logo palette from looks.css:247) and regenerate. The rest SVG and the .riv come from the same numbers, so the swap stays invisible. Update the contract's change log.
elements.a11y: Decorative and aria-hidden. Meaning is carried by the form's status/alert. Keyboard focus drives the same states as the pointer.
elements.risks: If the contact sheet is a transformed (3D) layer, the canvas inside a transformed parent still works, but resizeDrawingSurfaceToCanvas must follow scale changes. Avoid scaling the parent after load, or the canvas renders blurry (a scaled bitmap). Changing artboard size or names breaks the contract probe. The colours must stay brand-correct: Horizon colours only from the logo palette.

elements.name: LeadModal plus lead-intent: the lead popup
elements.what: Opens on intent, never on a timer (D79, LeadModal.tsx:30-53). lead-intent.js scores distinct signals: engaged-reading (25s active and 45% depth), interest-* (8s active dwell on each [data-intent=interest] covering half the screen), considering (2 uses of [data-intent-signal]), came-back (tab hidden 20s or more with 30% or more depth), scroll-back (1.5 viewports up within 1s after half the page). It opens at 2 points, or on a strong signal: desktop exit intent, or reading [data-intent=end] then scrolling back up. Never before 12s active. Pending opens wait up to 20s for a calm moment: not scrolling (0.9s), no anchor jump (1.5s), no keyboard nav (4s), not typing, no keyboard-focused control, contact not in view (30% coverage), no aria-modal dialog open, and isBusy (body.mw-consent-open) false. Conversions (wa.me/tel/mailto clicks, any submit) stop it forever (localStorage leadIntent.converted). Dismissal gives session quiet plus a 3-day cooldown. QA switches: ?lead=off|now|debug. UI: div.lm fixed inset 0 z-60 with a 0.55 black backdrop (click closes) and a .lm__card role=dialog aria-modal (max-width 440, max-height 100svh-32px, ground/ink tokens). Contents: close button (44px, aria 'סגירת החלון'), h3 title, a 112px .lm__face Lottie '/animations/13 Leave Details/contact us.json', name and phone fields, a privacy checkbox (27px) with label, error/failure lines, and LookButton 'תחזרו אליי' with states. Submit: with no endpoint it opens WhatsApp prefilled ('היי, אני {name} ואשמח לשיחת ייעוץ ללא עלות.\nטלפון: {phone}') and closes after 4s; with an endpoint it POSTs, sets localStorage leadModalSubmitted, shows success and closes after 3s.

The diagnosis measured it covering the story from mid-scroll under the old timer; the intent logic now blocks it while scrolling. The privacy label is 0.9rem (16.2px, at the limit). On phones there is no exit intent, so the strong signal is read-to-footer then a fast scroll up.

elements.name: ScrollEngineProvider + useScene / useMotionEngine (React bridge)
elements.what: Creates one engine per accessibility state (line 41: createMotionEngine({gsap,ScrollTrigger,SplitText,Lenis},{reduce:!ambient})). It toggles html.motion-calm (lines 43-45), re-measures when the body height changes through a ResizeObserver plus safeRefresh (lines 52-65), lands deep links once fonts are in (lines 69-80), and resets scroll on route change (lines 83-93). useScene (lines 108-122) runs a setup inside useGSAP with revertOnUpdate, skips it under PRERENDER, and re-runs every scene when the engine is swapped.
elements.mobile: No change is needed for 390. Lenis never runs on touch (syncTouch:false), so phones scroll natively and only the scrubbed transforms move. Lazy sheets that mount later trigger the ResizeObserver refresh, which is what keeps a long one-shot page in sync after Suspense chunks arrive.
elements.reduced: The accessibility widget's 'stop animations' (html.disable-animations) gives ambient=false, which builds a REDUCE engine; every useScene re-runs and scenes return early. With the OS flag, CALM: html.motion-calm is set and scenes still scrub with small travel. ?motion=full lifts CALM.
elements.perf: Ships in the 'motion-engine' manualChunk (vite.config.ts line 63: gsap, @gsap/react, lenis). One ResizeObserver on body. It costs nothing extra per scene.
elements.api: <ScrollEngineProvider> (already wraps all routes in App.tsx line 121). useScene<T>((engine, root) => cleanup?, deps) returns a ref. useMotionEngine() returns the engine or null.
elements.reuse_in_one_shot: This is the camera rig for the whole shot. Every chapter of the shot (hero dive, landing sheets, desk objects, pull-back) is one useScene on its own section, exactly as ProtoC.tsx does at lines 31, 76 and 113. No new provider is needed. Mobile first: write each scene's REDUCE early return first, then the CALM small-tilt values, then full.
elements.risks: In a shot page every sheet owns a scene, so a missing return/cleanup leaks triggers across StrictMode double mounts. Keep all gsap work inside the setup closure, which useGSAP reverts.

elements.name: createMotionEngine policy flags (REDUCE / CALM / FINE / RTL / DIR, ?reduce, ?motion=full, ?at)
elements.what: REDUCE = PRERENDER or ?reduce=1 or options.reduce or html[data-motion=off] or html.disable-animations (lines 44-45). CALM = OS prefers-reduced-motion unless ?motion=full (lines 46-47); it means no Lenis, getVelocity() returns 0, and reveal() runs with y=0. FINE = hover and fine pointer (line 48). DIR is 1 in RTL. html.motion-ready / motion-reduced are toggled at boot (lines 171-172) and never written into the prerender snapshot. ?at=<px>|<id>:<0..1> jumps to a scene state for screenshots (lines 297-322).
elements.mobile: FINE is false on phones, so pointer parallax on desk objects must be gated on FINE. ScrollTrigger.config({ignoreMobileResize:true}) (line 57) and onWidthResize (lines 82-92) mean the address bar showing or hiding never rebuilds the dive mid-gesture.
elements.reduced: REDUCE: no hidden states and no transforms; scenes render their last frame, so the shot must read as a plain list of flat sheets. CALM (DECISIONS #47, Nati's own Windows reports reduce): the camera still follows scroll, with small angles (ProtoC uses rotateX 10 instead of 30, and scrub:true instead of 0.6).
elements.perf: Lenis runs on gsap.ticker with lagSmoothing(0), desktop only. A velocity trigger runs on every page.
elements.api: engine.REDUCE, CALM, FINE, RTL, DIR, PRERENDER, fontsReady, scene(), splitLines(), holdTimeline(), reveal(), playInView(), getVelocity(), safeRefresh(), onWidthResize(), lock()/unlock(), scrollTo(), destroy(). Types in motion-engine.d.ts lines 51-80.
elements.reuse_in_one_shot: The three-tier camera: full = dive and tilt; CALM = the same path with angles divided by about 3 and no velocity skew; REDUCE = the camera stays at eye level (sheets flat, desk objects in place). Give every shot hold an id (holdTimeline(wrapper,{id:'dive'}), and likewise 'objects', 'pullback') so ?at=dive:0.5 films the 390 frames deterministically. ProtoC already uses 'dive' and 'pullback'.

Shared CSS is at looks.css lines 296-297: html.motion-ready .hold { height: var(--hold-h, 500svh) } and .hold__stage { position: sticky; top: var(--head); height: calc(100svh - var(--head)); overflow: clip }. elements.reduced: The height and sticky rules apply only under html.motion-ready, so REDUCE and prerender get a normal-height section showing the final frame.
elements.perf: Sticky plus progress-only means zero layout shift (memory: GSAP pin causes CLS). Scrub 0.6 desktop, true under CALM.
